📹Yemen's Saudi-backed forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandab as Houthis tighten their grip on the strait
Yemen's Southern Armed Forces announced that they were withdrawing from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area west of Taiz province, redeploying toward Aden as Houthi forces press south along the Red Sea coast.
The force described the move as a military adjustment to reinforce Aden's defenses and reorganize front lines, though it effectively cedes the strategic chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
The withdrawal follows weeks of fighting after Ansar Allah launched an offensive along Yemen's western coast in September. Government forces had attempted a [counteroffensive](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75636) in October to retake coastal territory, but the advances around [Taiz undermined](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76362) that effort.

events.text:
🇮🇱 Netanyahu and Eisenkot hold unity talks as Israeli coalition deadline looms
Negotiating teams for Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party met on Sunday evening to discuss a potential national unity government, even as the two leaders traded accusations over who was playing politics with the offer, Ynet reports.
Netanyahu publicly urged Eisenkot to enter talks "without preconditions," while Eisenkot dismissed the appeal as "another spin" and pointed out that the meeting had already been scheduled before Netanyahu's statement. He added Likud could join an emergency government under his leadership, but only if it accepts his principles and distances itself from right-wing forces.
The talks come with a hard deadline, as Eisenkot has 28 days to assemble a ruling coalition, with a possible 14-day extension. If he fails, another lawmaker could be given the chance, and a new election remains possible. Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has enough seats to form a government without a coalition with other parties.

🚨 Two tankers catch fire after striking naval mines in Hormuz – IRGC
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy released footage showing two oil tankers exploding after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Both vessels caught fire, and one, a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil, sank in the southern Persian Gulf.
The IRGC said the tankers switched off their tracking and identification systems and tried to cross via the southern route without Iranian clearance. It accused the US military of supporting the attempt.
Earlier in the day, the IRGC said [the two tankers struck mines](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77786) and caught fire, and that two other vessels turned back into the Persian Gulf after their naval traffic control center warned them in the wake of the blasts. The blasts are the latest in a series of incidents in which vessels have struck mines or been forced to turn back since Iran imposed its transit restrictions.

🪖🇮🇱 Israeli military activity in Syria surges, with dozens of incursions reported in recent weeks
A war monitor has counted at least 70 IDF incursions in southern Syria in the first two weeks of November, including probing patrols, construction of checkpoints, blocking of local roads using earthen barriers and behavior matching that of an occupying administration, including searches of homes and civilian ID checks.
👉Since November 1,[ IDF activity has been reported in Quneitra and Daraa provinces](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74362), and the strategic Mount Hermon in the Damascus countryside, according to the so-called Syrian Observatory for Human Rights.
Quneitra residents held a protest Friday demanding the release of kidnapped relatives held in Israeli prisons. Ex-detainees and relatives have told LA Times captives face beatings, threats and harsh conditions, with no explanation about why they’re being held.
➡️ Separately on Friday, SANA reported that Israeli forces had entered the town of Jabata al-Khashab, Quneitra, temporarily detaining three people, searching homes and damaging shops.
On Sunday, Israeli tanks opened fire on agricultural lands and fields in the western Daraa countryside. No casualties were reported, and no details given about what caused the incident.
Syria’s government has formally demanded that Israel withdraw from its internationally-recognized territories, but not issued any new statements on November’s escalating incursions. Families told LA Times their appeals to the government about getting their loved ones back “have fallen on deaf ears.”
December will mark the second anniversary of the surprise collapse of the Assad government and its replacement by rebel forces. During the chaos in 2024, Israel launched hundreds of air, artillery and drone attacks to destroy Syria’s air defense, air force, navy and missile forces, and added ~400 sq. km to the territories it’s occupied since 1967. Last month, Etana Syria estimated that Israeli incursions take place across an additional ~1,160 sq km.

events.text:
🚨🇮🇷 Iran says it’s in ‘neither-war-nor-peace’ state: what does that mean?
 
[Iran’s parliament speaker reiterated](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77797) Sunday that Tehran would not be bullied by Washington into a binary choice of talks on US terms or war, and that the prevailing third option – a “state of neither war nor peace,” could be brought to an end if the US meets Iran’s criteria for negotiations.
Iran’s [usage of the “neither war nor peace” ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69980)(na jang, na solh) concept dates back to the Iran-Iraq War of 1980-1988, and the 1988 ceasefire that saw a halt in fighting without a formal peace treaty or resolution of underlying disputes. However, the ‘cold war’-style dynamics of armed truces combined with localized fighting goes back thousands of years to the ancient Persian-Roman rivalry spanning from the late first century BC through the seventh century AD.
Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei revived the concept and the related idea of “no war, [no negotiation” during Trump’s 2018-2020 ‘maximum pressure’ campaign](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69009), which saw the US withdraw from the nuclear deal, reintroduction of tough sanctions, tit-for-tat tanker seizures, proxy attacks, terror designations, the downing of an American spy drone over Hormuz, the US assassination of one of the IRGC’s top commanders, and retaliatory Iranian missile strikes on US bases in Iraq.
“Neither war nor peace” returned after the breakdown of the Iran-US MoU in July 2026. In current realities, it means:
♦️ a lack of full-scale warfare, combined with mutual hostility and occasional back-and-forth strikes
♦️ a dual-blockade war of attrition in and around Hormuz
♦️[ an Iranian “seven conditions” ultimatum ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77587)(an end to hostilities across the region, lifting of US sanctions, withdrawal of US forces, war reparations) before talks can resume, given how many times the US and Israel have struck in the middle of negotiations
♦️[ ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77587)the prospect of expanding the war’s geography, scope and sophistication if the [US attacks again](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77405) or rejects and honorable peace
